citation.authors: Burley MJ, Wall BT, Bond B, Williams CA, Monteyne AJ, Stephens FB
citation.title: Acute and chronic application of novel incremental breath-hold technique increases endurance exercise performance in healthy men and male military personnel

population.description: Study A: eleven healthy male participants (age 28.5 +/- 6.9 y, height 178.3 +/- 5.2 cm, weight 84.7 +/- 7.1 kg); non-smokers without cardiovascular, neurological, respiratory or metabolic disease. BMI is not printed and not computed.

protocols.name: control_rest_baseline
protocols.description: Study A control (CON) visit, baseline sample only: participants arrived 'following a 2 h fast' (Methods); what they ate before it is not printed, so the arm starts from typical values (init norm_center) rather than from a spun-up fed day, and the 2 h is not entered (the arm's minute 0 is also later than arrival: cannula and face mask were fitted first, for an unprinted time). They rested semi-supine for 20 min and the baseline sample was taken at the end of that rest, before the 40 min of CON rest and the cycling. Minute 0 is the start of the 20 min quiet rest, so the baseline is minute 20 and the arm runs to 21. Only the baseline value is entered; the later 40 min rest, the 15 min steady-state cycling at 80% VO2max and the 5 min time trial are not, because the group's VO2max is not printed. The clock hour is not printed.

findings.description: Baseline heart rate of the control (rest) visit, semi-supine after 20 min of rest, before the 40 min control period

location.where: Results, Study A cardiorespiratory variables, paragraph on HR (Figure 1d); all values mean +/- SD (Methods, statistics)
location.quote: Baseline HR (Figure 1d) was similar between CON (66 ± 10 bpm)
